p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing D-beta-hydroxybutyrate as a fuel. It begins with D-beta-hydroxybutyrate, where C bonds left to CH3, up to OH, down to H, and right to CH2, which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. Below this are reversible arrows, identified as D-beta-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right is a curved arrow from NAD+ pointing to NADH [plus] H+. These arrows point to acetoacetate, where C bonds left to CH3, double bonds up to O, and right to CH2, which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. Below this is an arrow pointing down to acetoacetyl-CoA, identified as beta-ketoacyl-CoA transferase. To the right of the arrow is succinyl-CoA (in a pink box) pointing to succinate (in a red box) with a curved arrow. Acetoacetyl-CoA begins with C, which bonds left to CH3, double bonds up to O, and right to CH2, which bonds to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA (in a red box). Reversible arrows, identified as thiolase (in blue), are below this. CoA-SH (in a blue box) joins the down arrow. Below this is 2 acetyl-CoA, where C bonds left to CH3, double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA (in a blue box). To the right of this is a plus sign. To the right of this is C bonding left to CH3, double bonding up and right to O, and bonding down and right to S-CoA (in a pink box).
